title: Backlog
description: A stated scope broken into epics and task contracts, each with one objective, its dependencies, and the criteria that decide it is done. Order is not a field: foundation/0004 R3 has order follow from what each unit declares it requires, so a consumer derives it from dependencies rather than reading a sequence somebody asserted. No estimate and no priority either — both were carried by the source agent, and both are judgements about the project rather than about the unit of work. The contract encodes no numeric bound on task or backlog size: foundation/0006 R21 admits only a calibrated threshold, and a caller who wants one supplies it per run.

backlog_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

scope.description: The scope as the caller stated it, carried forward verbatim. A backlog read apart from the scope it decomposes cannot be checked for what it left out.

area.description: The part of the scope this epic answers. An epic holds no work of its own.

id.description: Sequential across the backlog rather than per epic, so a cross-reference resolves without knowing which epic holds it.

epic.description: Exactly one. A task in two epics has two reasons to exist.

objective.description: One sentence stating what must exist afterwards. An 'and' joining two outcomes is two tasks.

origin.description: What in the scope or specification this answers. A task with no origin is one nobody asked for.

dependencies.description: Tasks that must be demonstrable first. Cannot-be-demonstrated-before, never would-be-convenient-after. A cycle is rejected at the boundary; the producer resolves it rather than recording it.

criteria.description: What would show the task is done, each independently checkable and stated as an observable rather than an activity.

open_questions.description: Every reading the scope leaves open, and every element of the scope no task answers. Required rather than optional: an empty array is a claim that the scope was fully decomposed, and it should be made deliberately.
